visual_blocks.heading: RAPID REVISION 4 - Equality III: 'Equality of What?' -- Sen, Cohen and Dworkin
visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Capability = utility, or capability = income. Both are wrong.

visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Saying Berlin rejects positive liberty outright.

visual_blocks.heading: RAPID REVISION 6 - Liberty II: Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Green and the Liberty-Equality Relation
visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Treating liberty and equality as permanent, level-independent enemies.

visual_blocks.heading: RAPID REVISION 7 - Liberty III: Technological Society and Republican Non-Domination
visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Confusing an un-interfered-with dependent with a free person.

visual_blocks.heading: RAPID REVISION 8 - Justice I: Meaning, Plato, Aristotle, the Criteria Problem and Corrective Justice
visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Reducing justice to "whatever the law says"; legality is not legitimacy.

visual_blocks.heading: RAPID REVISION 9 - Justice II: Rawls, Nozick, Sen, Ambedkar and the Ordering Verdict
visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: "Rawls's first principle is equality." It is equal LIBERTY (lexically prior).

visual_blocks.preview: WRONG: Two-biography comparisons and one-sided demolitions.

visual_blocks.heading: 9.1 10-mark method (~150 words · 4 moves · ~12 minutes)

visual_blocks.preview: ⚠️ For "compare/distinguish" stems, insert one 3-axis table here. For "how far" stems, the conditional verdict is the mark-bearing move and must be at least three lines.

visual_blocks.heading: ORIGINAL MCQ MASTERY SET - EXACTLY 48 QUESTIONS
visual_blocks.preview: Questions 1-40 are core coverage - four per subtopic across the ten subtopics; Questions 41-48 are remedial items targeting the most common misreadings. Correct answers rotate strictly A -> B -> C -> D 12 times.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 1 - The Ideals Triad: Map, Working Thesis and the Ordering Problem
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Composite spine -> name the two ideals -> show each is indeterminate alone -> bring in justice as the ordering criterion -> graded verdict that concedes something to the losing side.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 2 - Equality I: Equal Worth, the Four Forms, Opportunity vs Outcome
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Equality spine -> equal worth (not sameness) -> name the relevant form (legal / political / social / economic) -> opportunity vs outcome -> which criterion, and why, is the mark-bearing move.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 3 - Equality II: Rousseau, Mill and Marx on Inequality, Individuality and Need
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Do not import the Marx-as-ideology answer here; the demand is the equity/equality DISTINCTION, framed by Marx.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 4 - Equality III: 'Equality of What?' -- Sen, Cohen and Dworkin
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: If a stem treats equality as one flat thing, win marks by asking "equality of what -- welfare, resources or capabilities?" and naming Sen.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 5 - Liberty I: Meaning, Berlin's Two Concepts, Mill's Harm Principle
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: 10-mark liberty spine -> negative/positive distinction -> Berlin's warning OR Mill's harm gate -> one evidence unit -> graded verdict.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 6 - Liberty II: Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Green and the Liberty-Equality Relation
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: "How far" = degree judgment compulsory. Name the conditions under which liberty limits equality and the conditions under which they reinforce.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 7 - Liberty III: Technological Society and Republican Non-Domination
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: On any liberty-vs-equality stem, deploy non-domination to show that certain equalisations are freedom-INCREASING, not freedom-reducing.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 8 - Justice I: Meaning, Plato, Aristotle, the Criteria Problem and Corrective Justice
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Justice-first distinction = proportional (distributive) vs arithmetic (corrective); then name the criterion for the specific good in dispute.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 9 - Justice II: Rawls, Nozick, Sen, Ambedkar and the Ordering Verdict
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: For "is X an improvement upon Y?", the criterion of improvement must be named BEFORE you apply it.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 10 - Debates, Criticisms and Traps: Synthesis Across the Triad
visual_blocks.preview: MEMORY: Directive first. "Discuss" = expose one live tension; "critically evaluate" = objection-reply is the answer; "how far" = degree judgment; "is X an improvement?" = name the criterion first.

visual_blocks.heading: Practice Design
visual_blocks.preview: DIRECTIVE -> THESIS -> DOCTRINE -> NAMED SOURCE / EXAMPLE -> OBJECTION / REPLY -> VERDICT
